title: Distributed Systems in Go
summary: Retries and idempotency, quorum replication, term-based leader election, log replication, durable restarts and a replicated key-value store, all tested against seeded, deterministic failure schedules.
description: Distributed systems fail in ways a single process never does: messages are lost, duplicated and reordered, nodes crash and come back with only what they wrote to disk, and a network split leaves two halves that cannot see each other. This course builds the core ideas as small deterministic state machines in standard-library Go. You will make retried requests safe with idempotency, replicate a register with quorums, elect a leader with terms, replicate a log with the Raft-style consistency check, persist the right state so a restart cannot break a promise, and finish with a replicated key-value store. Nothing uses real networks or clocks. A hidden, seeded scheduler delivers, drops, duplicates and reorders messages, partitions the cluster and restarts nodes, and the tests assert safety invariants after every step across many different schedules.
outcomes: Reason about safety under message loss, duplication, partitions and restarts.
Build term-based leader election, log replication and durable recovery as deterministic state machines.
Check a replicated store against invariants across many seeded failure schedules.
